BEST_BET.rationale: The only step change on a mission axis that survived every red-team correction: energy per bit moved ~10x below HBM (0.37 vs 3.95 pJ/b delivered at SM-local placement; 5.5x worst case at random placement, 15x at 1 mm), ~92 W saved per backside-power GPU at the 16-tier x 1 b planning case (78 GB/GPU; 48-169 W range), refresh-light (1e-4-tail refresh ~3.6 s at 105 C, ~225x rarer than Si). 0 kills; the one FATAL objection (backside overlay) has a carrier-last design-around. The prize is sized to carry a $10-50M raise: at ~$16.4 per W saved over 5 yr, ~$1.5k per GPU, which covers the $4.6-12/GB near tier ~2x. It is not a cost-per-bit play, and that is fine. Operator re-score S4 x P4 x D3 = 48. It ties RAW-BER (S3 x P4 x D4 = 48) on the physics scale and wins the tie because RAW-BER is worth ~$3.9 per module and can be copied in firmware. It is ahead of PIXEL 36, CHARGE-RIVER 30, LEAN 30, MARGIN 24 (owner re-score), AND 24, DIODE 16, DIET 15 and CWF ~12. Execution fit: the cell question is settled with coupons plus a bench at Purdue/GT for ~$175-240k by M11, which two founders can run. The same oxide 2T0C tail data (write-FET tail, 2-b drift, cross-temperature) de-risks AND-STACK for free. Weakness: TSMC/Intel own the backside-power slot, so the raise needs a named BSPDN partner (Intel Foundry 18A/14A is the U.S. option).
BEST_BET.experiment: Gate A+ by M11 (2027-11-30). Vertical channel-all-around 2T0C coupons in IGZO, In-poor IGZO, IGO and ZTO; single vs series write gate; -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold. Each split is measured after the post-bond heat/H sequence AND a real D2O-labelled 350-400 C fusion bond. On >=1e5 cells per split: drift sigma at 1/10/100 s at 85/105/125 C; write-T1/read-T2 maps (dT +/-30 K) with in-row references; RTN from >=100 reads ~1 s apart plus 1 us-1 ms fast reads; the directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile; SIMS H/D and top-tier dVt. PASS 1 b: drift <=75 mV, RTN 1e-4 quantile <=100 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, bonded dVt <=10 mV (2 b upside: <=20 mV drift in a >=600 mV window, cross-T <=10 mV, RTN <=30 mV, tail <=7.5 aA at 105 C). Then Gate B (M18): RO shift <=1% and Vt <=10 mV under 2 oxide tiers on sky130-carrier logic, after a 1,000 h bake. Gate C (carrier emulation, CSAM, VPD-ICPMS In/Ga/Zn) becomes the raise milestone with a BSPDN partner.
BEST_BET.cost: ~$240k standalone to Gate A+ (~$175k marginal on the shared oxide-tails lot, plus metrology); ~$60k more for Gate B on the shared sky130 carrier. Standalone full plan $1.00M ($677k experiments).
BEST_BET.kill: Physics kills, 2027-11-30 (M11), on every split including the real-bond split. (1) Drift sigma >75 mV at 1 s/105 C that is still >75 mV when re-measured at a 100 ms hold: kill the capacity claim. (2) 1e-4-tail retention <1 s at 105 C (tail >22.5 aA), even with series write gates and -0.7 V hold: kill. (3) RTN 1e-4 quantile >100 mV in every vertical split: kill the capacity claim. (4) Drop 2 b permanently if window <600 mV, cross-T >10 mV, RTN >30 mV or tail >7.5 aA. 2028-06-30 (M18): kill the BEOL tiers (carrier-only) if RO shift >1% or Vt >10 mV is unrecoverable. Operator rule (not a kill): if no BSPDN foundry will host carrier emulation in-kind by M20, raise on the 1 b oxide near-tier cell plus <=4 BEOL tiers and keep the carrier as the partner milestone.

FASTEST_PROOF.rationale: Most decisive result per dollar and month in the portfolio. It needs no fab, starts in week 1 on bought hardware (DRAM Bender stations, retired DDR4, open Antmicro DDR5 RDIMM testers) and reaches a binary GO/NO-GO at M6 for ~$124k standalone (~$90k in the portfolio). The non-device founder can run it while the recruited device expert builds the oxide lot. It is the only concept that produces real data before the first coupon returns. The revised prize is real but modest: ~9x refresh energy on DDR5 RDIMMs at 85 C with chipkill kept (6-20x; ~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL), and 64Gb refresh-busy 18% -> 2%. Its portfolio value is larger. The error-geometry census (iid vs row-correlated/VRT, pairs <1%, multi-chip share) is the measured basis for the 1.88x ECC margin that MARGIN-STACK, PIXEL-STACK, HOT-SIDE's concatenated ECC and AND-STACK's 2-b MLC all bank on. If errors at 1e-4 are mostly correlated, every new-cell margin budget tightens, and we learn that at M6, not M17. The flag leg is already killed, so this is a clean refresh/coding test. Runner-up for cheapest kill: CHARGE-RIVER GATE 1 (M10, ~$40k as a lot rider, P ~10-20%), after a $0 read of imec's CTE papers in week 1.
FASTEST_PROOF.experiment: Phase 1 (M0-6). (a) 150 retired DDR4 modules screened across >=30 lots/vendor and 60 deep-mapped across 1x-1a date codes on DRAM Bender: retention at 0.128-4 s x 45/65/85 C x 4 patterns, with the cluster spectrum scored under RS-8 and BCH-12. (b) >=24 DDR5 1a/1b RDIMMs on open Antmicro testers: JEDEC ECS singleton counts plus post-SEC event maps with BEER-style H-matrix recovery, giving the RS-8-behind-SEC safe interval. (c) VRT arrival counts at 1 s/85 C over 1,000 h on 20 modules, plus a dwell-time spectrum. (d) Failure-mode census by chip/DQ/beat/row/column/MAT. (e) The 1 h grade must hold over 1,000 h. (f) Hammer at relaxed refresh with controller RFM. Shared output: the reduced-charge pair study MARGIN-STACK needs (pairs <1%). GO: RS-8 safe interval incl. VRT >=6x the JEDEC window at 85 C (DDR5 >=0.19 s, DDR4 >=0.38 s) and >=24x at 65 C; multi-chip events <=10%; 1 h grade holds for >=95% of modules.
FASTEST_PROOF.cost: ~$124k standalone Phase 1 (~$90k in the portfolio, 2-3 stations, shared with the MARGIN-STACK pair study); the controller and soak phases ($946k standalone) are deferred to a partner or the raise.
FASTEST_PROOF.kill: M6 (2027-06-30). Kill the commodity relaxed-refresh product if the RS-8 safe interval incl. VRT is <4x the JEDEC window at 65 C (<256 ms DDR4, <128 ms DDR5). Kill binary BCH if >0.4% of error bits arrive in >=3-bit clusters; kill both line codes if >10% of events span >1 byte. Kill the DDR5 claim (keep retired DDR4) if the RS-8-behind-SEC interval is <4x 32 ms at 65 C. M9: kill the 85 C claim if VRT growth stops a 10-min scrub from holding >=0.5 s. Portfolio consequence of a kill: every new cell drops the 1.88x ECC margin from its budget (Cs planning cases go up).

MOONSHOT.rationale: Highest ceiling if it works. It is the only concept whose density comes from tier count on NAND-class tools with one hole etch and no EUV in the array. Revised: 64 tiers x 2 b = 2.62 Gb/mm2, 5.9x 1-beta (was 8.1x); bits/$ ~2.3x vs 2026 1-beta (2.2-2.6x); ~1.1-1.4x vs a projected 2032 incumbent at first product and 1.2-1.6x at 96 tiers in two decks; refresh ~25x lower at 1 s retention. Tiers can keep climbing the way NAND's did. With PIXEL-STACK it carries the portfolio's only >=2x bits/$ case, and PIXEL lands at ~parity bits/$ (4.6x density). The odds are honest-low. The single-film closure is topologically impossible (killed), and the two-film notched write pocket has P(closure) ~20% and needs three unprecedented modules. NEO is ~3 years ahead on NAND-process DRAM, and Macronix holds a 3D AND pillar estate. Operator re-score S4 x P2 x D3 = 24. Why it belongs in a $1M seed: its cell physics is the same oxide 2T0C that the HOT-SIDE lot already measures (write-FET hold tail, 2-b drift, cross-T), so the planar statistics ride for ~$15k. Only the TCAD plus the 2-tier closure coupon (~$110k) is incremental, and it is released only after two cheap gates.
MOONSHOT.experiment: G0 TCAD (M0-3): a notch geometry with >=9 decades of write-segment suppression at a -3.0 V hold (120 mV/dec plus DIBL) and nominal CR >=0.55. #1A planar on the shared lot (M9): CR >=0.57 at within-tier sigma <=0.045 over >=50 cells; <=111 fA per unselected cell; write-FET 1e-4 hold tail <=17 aA on >=1e4 devices at 85 C; 4 levels holding >=1 s at 85 C with <=78 mV tail drift; cross-T 2-b BER <=1e-4 at dT +/-10 K. #1B (M14-16): a 2-tier vertical closure coupon with 250 nm e-beam holes in SiO2/poly-SiGe/SiO2/SiN, built as the two-film notched write pocket. It must show write-then-read on >=2 tiers with no ring-to-read-channel short, ring hold <=100 aA at 85 C with the write plate at -3.0 V, per-tier CR >=0.57, and FIB/TEM of the notch contact.
MOONSHOT.cost: ~$0.4M direct to GO #1B standalone ($970k full plan); in this portfolio ~$125k incremental ($15k lot rider + $110k TCAD and closure coupon). The 32-tier dummy-stack etch coupon and the 4-tier stack are raise or NAND-partner milestones.
MOONSHOT.kill: M3: G0 TCAD fails (no notch geometry reaches 9 decades or CR >=0.55): move to the coaxial/per-tier fallback (~1.0-1.6x bits/$, no seed money). M9 (2027-09-30): CR mean <0.40 or sigma >0.07: kill single-etch. Write-FET 1e-4 tail >1 fA or ring tail >1 fA at 85 C: kill the DRAM-class claim (>100 aA drops 2 b). 63-cell on/off <1e4 at <=3.5 V: kill. M18 (2028-06-30): no write-then-read closure on >=2 tiers, or notch-segment hold >1 fA: kill the single-etch leg and the bits/$ step claim. A blocking Macronix/NEO patent or a failed dummy etch is a pivot to a JDA, not a kill.

sequence: M0 (Jan 2027), week 1: incorporate and file 2 provisionals before any disclosure (hot-side bond-H control and cross-T MLC; AND notched write pocket). Read imec's IGZO CCD CTE papers ($0); CHARGE-RIVER gets no fab money until P is restated. Sign Purdue Birck and GT IEN external-user agreements. File the Argonne XPS/SIMS user proposal. Order the DRAM Bender stations and the modules.

M0-6: RAW-BER Phase 1 error census on DDR4 and DDR5, run by the systems founder (~$90k). It doubles as MARGIN-STACK's pair study. Errors at 1e-4 are classed iid vs correlated: the ECC-margin input for every cell.

M0-3: desk work (TCAD/SPICE/field solver, ~$0 beyond licences). AND G0 notch TCAD; MARGIN field-solver alpha on published VCT geometry; HOT-SIDE capacity-indexed trace study and claim reading; mask design for ONE shared oxide-tails lot.

M2-10: ONE shared oxide-tails lot at Purdue/GT (~$210k + $80k riders + $60k metrology). Splits: IGZO / In-poor IGZO / IGO / ZTO / Ga-free In2O3 (Ga export ban suspension ends 2026-11-27). Arrays: >=1e5-1e6 floating-node 2T leakage cells, single vs series write gate (I-12627), -0.5/-0.7 V hold; a 65k-node small-area (<=0.02 um2) SF RTN array with on-coupon 15 ns dual S/H; drift and cross-T maps at 85/105/125 C; 1x/2x/4x cumulative H/thermal dose; a D2O-labelled real-bond split. Riders: AND planar CR/disturb cells; overlapping-gate planar CCDs (only if the imec read passes); pixel lateral-cavity capacitors; RuO2/MoOx Schottky anode splits for DIODE-TOWER. This one RTN and leakage campaign serves HOT-SIDE (tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, RTN <=100 mV), PIXEL (residual <=40 mV, tail <=90 aA), MARGIN (2e-5 quantile <=586 aA, RTN <=44 mV), AND (write-FET tail <=17 aA), CHARGE-RIVER readout (SF RTN <=30 e-) and DIODE-TOWER readout.

M2-9: ONE ChipFoundry SkyWater sky130 shuttle, post-processed with BEOL IGZO (~$80k). IGZO gain FETs drive on-chip fF nodes sampled at 1-3 ns, the RTN timescale that MARGIN, PIXEL and CHARGE-RIVER need and benches cannot reach. Ring-oscillator/Vt monitors on the same die later serve as HOT-SIDE Gate B's logic host. This replaces the $275k 22FDX MPW, which the red team showed cannot measure alpha or oxide RTN.
M9-11: read the lot. PIXEL read/retention gate and AND #1A at M9, CHARGE-RIVER GATE 1 at M10, HOT-SIDE Gate A+ at M11.

M12: choose the lead and reallocate. HOT-SIDE if A+ passes at 1 b. If A+ fails but PIXEL reads <=40 mV, PIXEL leads toward its 4-tier stack. If both fail, publish the oxide-tails dataset, keep RAW-BER plus the readout IP, and re-plan. Open Intel Foundry 18A/14A and TSMC A16 BSPDN talks with A+ data in hand.
M12-16: AND 2-tier closure coupon (~$110k), released only if G0 and #1A passed. 1,000 h 105 C hold-bias stress on the lot (MARGIN aged 2e-5 quantile; HOT-SIDE bonded drift).
M14-18: HOT-SIDE Gate B. Two oxide tiers on the sky130-carrier logic plus a 1,000 h bake. PIXEL lateral capacitor after 4x 400 C.

M18-24: data room and raise ($10-50M). Lead: a 1 b near-tier cell at 125 C after a real bond, logic compatibility, a measured-input energy model (~10x vs HBM, ~90 W/GPU) and a BSPDN partner LOI for Gate C carrier emulation. Series A milestones: Gate C, PIXEL/AND 4-tier stacks, 22FDX readout MPW, CELL-WAFER bond vehicles. LEAN ARRAY MODULE goes to a Lam/AMAT/TEL JDA or a grant from day 1 at no seed cash. AI-MEMORY-DIET is published, not funded.
gates: G-M0 spend gate: no CHARGE-RIVER fab spend until imec's CTE definition is read. If the 98% is per transfer and buried gave <2x, the CCD rider is dropped and its $40k returns to contingency.

G-M3 desk gate: AND TCAD (>=9 decades write suppression at -3.0 V, CR >=0.55), else AND goes to the fallback and its $110k moves to HOT-SIDE Gate B / contingency. MARGIN field-solver alpha <=0.25, else MARGIN becomes instrument-only.

G-M6 RAW-BER GO/NO-GO: RS-8 safe interval incl. VRT >=6x the JEDEC window at 85 C (DDR5 >=0.19 s), multi-chip <=10%, 1 h grade holds >=95%. Kill if <4x at 65 C. Pairs <1% confirms the 1.88x ECC margin for all cells.

G-M9 lot read gate. PIXEL joint 2e-7 residual: <=20 mV GO (0.45 fF), <=40 mV PLAN (0.60 fF), >55 mV kills the oxide amp tier. Fast-trap SFs >8 mV <=3%. Tail <=90 aA after 4x dose. AND #1A: CR >=0.57, sigma <=0.045; kill if CR <0.40. Write-FET 1e-4 tail: <=17 aA; >1 fA kills.
G-M10 CHARGE-RIVER GATE 1: median CTE >=0.9973 at >=150 MT/s with DFE on the overlapping-gate reference, and buried deferral >=3x below surface. Kill if <0.9951.
G-M11 HOT-SIDE Gate A+ (company-defining). 1 b: drift <=75 mV, RTN 1e-4 quantile <=100 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, bonded dVt <=10 mV. 2 b upside: <=20 mV / <=10 mV cross-T / <=30 mV RTN / <=7.5 aA.
G-M12 lead selection and budget re-cut (see sequence). Remaining cash goes >=70% to the lead.
G-M16 AND GO #1B: 2-tier write-then-read closure, ring hold <=100 aA at 85 C, CR >=0.57. MARGIN aged 2e-5 leakage <=586 aA after 1,000 h at 105 C (NO-GO above the 1.0 fF limit).
G-M18 HOT-SIDE Gate B: RO shift <=1%, Vt <=10 mV under 2 tiers, else carrier-only. AND single-etch kill if no closure on >=2 tiers.
G-M22-24 raise gate: one cell passed with measured tails, plus a named partner (BSPDN foundry for HOT-SIDE, or a 3D-DRAM/NAND maker for PIXEL/AND).

honest_framing: From 10,525 distinct ideas, nothing survived as a free lunch: all 10 finalists were downgraded and none was killed. The downgrades came almost entirely from two places, not from broken physics: the statistical tails of deposited oxide transistors (aA leakage quantiles, ns-to-s RTN, hydrogen drift) and process modules no one has built. The real openings are where the incumbent's limit is the context, not the cell. Energy per bit moved next to compute (HOT-SIDE, ~10x vs HBM, survived every correction), refresh bought with coding (~9x on today's DDR5) and density from tier count instead of lithography (AND/PIXEL, 4.6-5.9x 1-beta) all hold up. But once yield and deck cost are priced, bits-per-dollar steps shrink to ~parity-1.6x against the 2032 incumbent, so 'cheaper DRAM' is not where a two-person team wins first. Persistence beats the engineering terms: every one of 181 objections got a numerical design-around (carrier-last, series write gates, muxed double sampling, chipkill-kept codes), and recruiting, partner access and process modules yield to grind. Persistence cannot move an oxide trap's emission time, a Schottky barrier or a 1e-5 leakage quantile; those must be measured, so the first ~$400k should turn them into numbers before anyone argues about markets.
biggest_unknown: Whether deposited oxide-semiconductor transistors (IGZO / IGO / ZTO / In2O3, <=400 C) have controllable tails at scale. That means the 1e-4 to 2e-5 quantiles of off-state leakage at the aA level, the RTN jump distribution from 1 ns to 1 s on <=0.02 um2 devices, and hydrogen/thermal drift after cumulative processing and a real bond, all on >=1e5-1e6 devices. The study's sources contain no such population data, and every surviving cell keys on it: HOT-SIDE tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C and RTN <=100 mV; PIXEL residual <=40 mV and tail <=90 aA; MARGIN 2e-5 quantile <=586 aA and RTN <=44 mV; AND write-FET tail <=17 aA; CHARGE-RIVER SF RTN <=30 e-. Most red-team downgrades were tail terms (2 b -> 1 b, 0.45 -> 0.60 fF, the 17-40x stretch withdrawn). With near-Gaussian tails, 3-4 cells live. With heavy tails, the portfolio collapses to RAW-BER plus a 1 b HOT-SIDE tier.
monday_action: In <=2 hours: (1) 60 min: write the one-page 'Oxide Tails Lot' spec as a table. Rows: device types (2T leakage cell single/series write gate, small-area SF with on-coupon 15 ns S/H, drift/cross-T structures, D2O real-bond split). Columns: channel splits (IGZO, In-poor IGZO, IGO, ZTO, Ga-free In2O3), array sizes (>=1e5-1e6 cells, 65k SFs), temperatures (85/105/125 C), sampling timescales (1-3 ns, 15 ns, 1 us-1 ms, 1 s) and each concept's pass line (17 / 22.5 / 90 / 586 aA; 30 / 44 / 100 mV). Copy every number from the dossiers' gates. (2) 40 min: email it as an RFQ and collaboration ask to the Purdue Birck external-user office and the Peide Ye group, and to Georgia Tech IEN and the Shimeng Yu / Asif Khan groups. Ask for price, a lot start date and any existing per-device 2T0C retention/RTN distributions. Send the same page to the top 3 device co-founder candidates as the technical pitch. (3) 20 min: order 2 DRAM Bender FPGA stations and the first 20 retired DDR4 RDIMMs so the fab-free RAW-BER census starts this month.
recruit_first: Co-founder #2, the recruited expert: an oxide-semiconductor device-reliability physicist (IGZO-class 2T0C cells, PBTI/hydrogen, RTN, aA floating-node leakage metrology, ALD splits) who can own the shared tails lot end-to-end. It is the critical path for BEST BET, MOONSHOT and PIXEL at once. Recruit from imec's IGZO 2T0C team alumni (G. S. Kar's group), Purdue (Peide Ye group), Georgia Tech (Shimeng Yu, Asif Khan and Suman Datta groups), Stanford (H.-S. Philip Wong / Krishna Saraswat groups), Intel Components Research and Micron Boise 3D-DRAM R&D. Recruiting reality: ~$65k/yr will not buy a senior industry person. Target a senior PhD or postdoc who has already run 2T0C retention arrays, and pay in co-founder equity plus first authorship on the first >=1e5-device oxide tails dataset. Top up with NSF SBIR / DoD Microelectronics Commons money. Second, by M6 as a contractor and hired after the raise: a CMOS image-sensor CDS readout designer from onsemi, OmniVision or Sony for the PIXEL/MARGIN readout. The non-expert founder covers systems/ECC and runs RAW-BER, with a DRAM Bender-experienced student subaward (SAFARI/ETH, Rutgers, Georgia Tech).
facility_first: Purdue Birck Nanotechnology Center (external-user agreement) for the shared oxide-tails lot: oxide ALD/sputter, e-beam, probing to 125 C, next to the Ye group's oxide-FET work. Georgia Tech IEN is the second source and backup. In parallel, file an Argonne user proposal (XPS band offsets, SIMS) and book a ChipFoundry SkyWater sky130 shuttle (Minnesota) for the BEOL-IGZO ns-sampling carrier, so the first-year demo is all U.S.
